record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can knowledge-base mapping generation tools generate useful mappings from mixed evidence that may be incomplete or incorrect, including source-to-target correspondences, source constraints, mined join paths, data examples, and automatically generated examples from the Linked Open Data cloud?

evidence.quote: An important research direction for KGMTs is mapping generation that can use incomplete or incorrect correspondences and data examples, perhaps leveraging automatically generated examples from the Linked Open Data (LOD) cloud.

artifact.status_search_result: This is an open research direction in data integration and knowledge-graph construction. Recent surveys on knowledge graph mapping tools (KGMTs), ontology-based data access, and tools such as Karma, BootOX, Mirror, and ML-based mapping generators indicate active ongoing work, but no general algorithm is known to robustly handle all five forms of mixed, possibly noisy evidence simultaneously. No definitive solution was found in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Knowledge Graph Construction Tools - survey
status_evidence.snippet: Mapping generation under incomplete or noisy correspondences remains an open challenge in knowledge graph construction.
status_evidence.claim: Mapping generation from incomplete/incorrect evidence is identified as an open challenge.
